subject: Request: network ownership exception for peered VPC (Sentinel Labs)
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice@sentinellabs.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sentinel Labs Procurement <procurement@sentinellabs.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: network ownership exception for peered VPC

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed, Sentinel Labs will be peering our VPC with Redwood Private for the initial rollout. Our security and networking teams have pushed back on allowing Redwood to accept a standard uptime SLA that covers the customer-owned networking layer.

We would like to request a formal exception to the availability SLA that acknowledges the following:

- Sentinel Labs retains ownership and operational responsibility for the peered network (VPN/Direct Connect/Customer router).
- Redwood will accept a limited SLA scope that excludes outages or latency degradation caused by customer-controlled network events (routing, single-VPC ISP outages, on-prem direct connect maintenance).
- Redwood will continue to provide best-effort support, runbook guidance, and telemetry integration for end-to-end diagnostics, but will not assume liability for third-party networking performance.

Attached are a short baseline metrics export and our network runbook for the peering setup (sentinel_availability_metrics.csv, network-runbook.pdf). Procurement copied me to start documenting the exception in the MSA.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can sign an explicit responsibility matrix that excludes customer-managed network incidents from uptime calculations, and if so, what the drafting language would look like? We'd like to avoid a lengthy legal back-and-forth.

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Head of Infrastructure
Sentinel Labs

Attachments: sentinel_availability_metrics.csv (CSV, 42KB), network-runbook.pdf (PDF, 380KB)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@sentinellabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: network ownership exception for peered VPC

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear summary and for sharing the runbook and baseline. Short answer: we can accommodate a scoped SLA that excludes customer-managed network incidents, provided both sides agree on a measurable responsibility matrix and diagnostic commitments (telemetry, packet captures, time-to-ack).

To move quickly I propose:
- Redwood will exclude incidents where root cause is in the customer-managed network (WAN, on-prem router, ISP) from availability uptime calculations for the Private deployment.
- Sentinel Labs will provide a primary contact and a network runbook + scheduled maintenance calendar.
- For any incident, the first step will be joint triage with timestamps; if the root cause is inconclusive within 24 hours we triage under the shared-investigation workflow (escalate to SRE).
- We will include a short clause in the MSA with sample language and an appendix (responsibility-matrix.xlsx) that both legal teams can redline.

Can you confirm Sentinel's point-of-contact for network ops and whether procurement prefers we draft the clause or if they'd like to propose language?

I'll loop Diego (SRE on Private infra) and Ben (your account lead) to draft the technical appendix and the initial clause.

Best,
Ava Chen
Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Monroe <alice@sentinellabs.com>, Sentinel Labs Procurement <procurement@sentinellabs.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed clause and responsibility matrix (Sentinel Labs)

Team —

Drafting note for the legal/ops teams. Below is proposed contract language we can send to Sentinel's counsel as a starting point. I would prefer we get internal legal eyes on this before sending the redline, but wanted to share the technical appendix concurrently so procurement has something concrete.

Proposed MSA language (technical summary):
"Redwood Inference's availability commitments for Private deployments exclude downtime or performance degradation caused solely by the Customer's network infrastructure, including but not limited to: Customer-managed WAN links, on-prem router failures, Customer ISP outages, and misconfiguration of Customer-controlled peering. Redwood will make reasonable efforts to assist in diagnosis and remediation but shall not be liable for credits or penalties for incidents attributed primarily to Customer-managed network components. Parties agree to maintain a responsibility matrix and diagnostic playbook to facilitate joint triage and root-cause determination."

Comments / operational controls:
- Add an appendix describing required telemetry (BGP session logs, traceroute results, packet captures on request) and expected timelines for providing data (48 hours for primary artifacts, 5 business days for deeper packet analysis).
- Proposed bullet: if joint triage cannot determine primary cause within 48 hours, incident remains in shared-investigation status and SLA calculations are paused for the period of investigation (documented timestamps).
- Redwood to provide a one-time onboarding run for network contact handoff and calendar integration for planned maintenances.

Attachments: proposed-responsibility-matrix.xlsx (contains sample classification matrix and incident timelines)

Next steps: legal to draft redline, ops to confirm telemetry requirements, Ben to coordinate with Sentinel procurement on whether they want to propose alternate language.

Diego Fernandez
SRE, Redwood Private

Attachments referenced: proposed-responsibility-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 22KB)
